headline: High-risk workspace leakage and cascading errors: Goose can write broadly while Notion AI shares workspace state and ingests user-accessible pages.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, while Notion AI operates over shared workspace pages. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text from one side can be reinterpreted by the other. The interaction is not fully documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Goose writes instructions into a shared file or page that Notion AI later summarizes
IF Notion AI ingests workspace text that originated from Goose without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep Goose and Notion AI on separate workspaces or folders
Add a manual review step before Notion AI consumes Goose-authored content
Disable MCP connectors that expose untrusted text to Goose
Use a naming convention for machine-generated pages and require human approval
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between filesystem and workspace content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in the current directory, and Notion AI can access pages and databases in the user’s workspace. If the same sensitive material is mirrored between those stores, both agents can expose it through their respective backends. The profiles show shared workspace state but not a guaranteed leak, so medium fits.
conditions: IF source code or secrets are copied into Notion pages accessible to Notion AI
IF Goose reads sensitive files that are later summarized or stored in the workspace
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared workspace pages
Restrict Goose to a non-sensitive repo clone
Separate code and knowledge workspaces
Review Notion page permissions before syncing content
requires-engineering: implement DLP/redaction before cross-tool copying

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and broad network egress; Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances. Even though Notion AI cannot write the host filesystem, both can mutate overlapping user-managed content, and Goose can also alter git state. The default overlap is dangerous and can cause conflicting edits or repository corruption.
conditions: IF Goose and Notion AI are both pointed at the same project artifacts or mirrored notes
IF Goose modifies git-tracked files while Notion AI edits the corresponding workspace copy
mitigations: Pause one agent before the other edits shared artifacts
Use separate branches for Goose-generated changes
Keep Notion AI out of git-tracked working directories
Manually reconcile diffs before syncing content
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency across workspace and repo

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it may treat Goose-produced text as authoritative if that text is copied into pages or databases. Goose can generate or modify those artifacts, creating a chain where one agent’s output becomes the other’s input without verification. The pathway exists in default workflows, but Notion AI is not shown to take irreversible actions.
conditions: IF Goose writes claims into files or pages that Notion AI later uses as grounding
IF Notion AI answers or drafts based on Goose-authored content without human verification
mitigations: Require human review of Goose outputs before importing them into Notion
Mark machine-generated notes as untrusted
Ask Notion AI to cite source pages explicitly
Keep factual claims in a separate reviewed page
requires-engineering: add verification gates between generation and workspace grounding

E_compliance.rationale: Goose is on-machine and handles local files, while Notion AI is vendor-hosted and uses Notion workspace permissions plus downstream model providers. That creates a residency and retention mismatch risk for workspace content, especially if regulated data is copied from local files into Notion. The profiles do not prove a specific legal violation, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data from Goose-managed files is pasted into Notion pages
IF the workspace contains data subject to stricter residency or retention rules than Notion’s vendor-hosted processing
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Notion
Use separate workspaces for sensitive content
Review Notion retention and export settings
Limit Goose to non-regulated repositories
requires-engineering: formalize a data-flow and residency policy for the pair
